Tree.argument: Complete binary trees indexed by depth, with equal-depth children; review the constructors and universe parameter.

constants.argument: The class is exactly the two constant Boolean functions, with arbitrary domain and no finiteness assumption.

BranchWise.argument: Deliberately defective comparator: unrestricted recursive classes permit a different witness at each level; the leaf is True.

PathConsistent.argument: Retain all earlier branch constraints by restricting the class at each edge; a leaf requires a concept witness.

repeated.argument: Repeat one arbitrary input at every internal node, at arbitrary natural-number depth.

branchWise_repeated.argument: Induction on depth supplies the true and false constant witnesses at each node, reusing the same unrestricted class.

uniform_no_positive.argument: For an arbitrary class whose functions all have fixed label b everywhere, the opposite root-label witness is impossible. Review both Bool cases, witness eliminations, and both local equalities.

true_restriction_uniform.argument: Membership in the constants and label true at one input eliminates the false constant. Review the function-equality case assumptions and the local contradiction.

constants_depth_le_one.argument: An arbitrary shattered tree of depth at least two has a positive-depth true subtree; its restricted class is uniform and therefore cannot shatter that subtree. Review the index case split and both local obligations.

constants_depth_one.argument: The chosen input and both constant functions witness depth one; review all four explicit witnesses, including restricted leaf membership.

constants_exact_depth.argument: Nonempty X supplies an input; combine the depth-one witness with the arbitrary-domain upper bound. No finite-domain enumeration is used.

repeated_counterexample.argument: The repeated-input depth-two tree satisfies the defective predicate but violates the repaired depth bound.

uniform_no_positive.have.1.argument: In the b=false branch, the true witness and uniformity give true=false.

uniform_no_positive.have.2.argument: In the b=true branch, the false witness and uniformity give false=true.

true_restriction_uniform.have.1.argument: Under the false-constant case assumption, membership in the true restriction gives false=true.

constants_depth_le_one.have.1.argument: Extract the true subtree obligation under the complete depth-at-least-two case.

constants_depth_le_one.have.2.argument: Apply the independently reviewed uniform-class obstruction to the positive-depth true subtree.

repeated_counterexample.have.1.argument: Assuming repaired shattering of the depth-two repeated tree yields the impossible numerical bound 2≤1.

open_obligations.statement: Construct and check a structure-preserving map from these standalone trees and predicates to the original project's tree, dimension, and mistake-bound interfaces.
Specify and prove an appropriate depth bound for concept classes beyond the two constants. The present theorem does not establish such a bound.

questions: Do complete depth-indexed trees and the selected Boolean branch directions express the intended objects?
Should the repaired leaf require a remaining concept witness, distinguishing empty from zero-dimensional nonempty classes?
Does cumulative restriction express the intended same-concept-per-path condition?
Are the arbitrary-domain upper bound, nonempty-domain lower witness, and all displayed local arguments acceptable with their complete contexts?
Which separate extension should be pursued next: transport to the original interfaces or a broader concept-class bound?
